subject: The entry threshold is set above what the scorer can produce -- the system has not been able to trade
body:
Two things from the finished calibration, and the second one is bigger than anything I built today.

FIRST -- your correction found a real effect.
Asking what the MOMENT looks like, instead of averaging a period into one number, immediately found
structure at z=-19 against a deflated bar of 3.95. Bars within 4 bars of a score sign flip (17.8% of
all bars) have IC -0.20/-0.31/-0.33 at h=1/3/5 against ~0.00 everywhere else, and the sign is
INVERTED -- right after a flip the score predicts the opposite of what it says. It survived every
attack I could build, including the time split. It gets STRONGER with conviction: -0.175 in the
lowest conviction quartile, -0.578 in the highest. The more sure it is at a flip moment, the more
wrong it is. The mechanism is the hit rate alone -- 31.2% vs 41.1% -- with the payoff geometry
identical between the two groups. That is your "win more often, lose less frequently", arriving from
the data instead of from the claim.

The honest limit: at the threshold the system actually trades, flip bars fall from 17.8% of all bars
to 2.7% of traded bars. The threshold was already filtering most of them. It does not rescue the
system. I nearly reported the +32R version of this before checking, and the checked version is much
smaller.

SECOND -- the system has not been able to open a trade.
Phase 3B ended 0 of 9 regimes validated, which is the standing outcome. The fallback then set every
regime threshold to 70, calling it "the P1 baseline". It is not. Phase 1 measured 40 this run, into a
local variable that is never written anywhere -- g_BaseThreshold is a hardcoded 70.0 that Phase 1
never touches.

And the live scorer's score CANNOT REACH 70. Across 50,000 exported bars its maximum is 52.07, with
6.5% of bars sitting at exactly that value -- a saturation ceiling, not a thin tail. The default
fallback threshold, 55, is also above it. The EA's own portal-audit measured this directly at the end
of the run: at the configured threshold the calibration scorer qualifies 110 bars out of 500 and the
live scorer qualifies ZERO. Agreement 0.0%.

That audit was shipped on August 5th and fires on every completed calibration. It printed "This is
the main thing to fix" today and, as far as I can tell, on every run before. The information was
never missing. It was unread.

What this means: a system that cannot open a trade looks exactly like a system that has chosen not
to. Every STAND DOWN in the record may have been reporting on entry being structurally impossible
rather than on edge being absent. The bar-level expectancy work is unaffected -- that runs on
exported scores, not on trades -- but the live record has been measuring something other than what
we thought.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not lower the threshold. At a reachable 40 the measured expectancy is
-0.0298R, so patching the constant would convert a silent halt into a losing system. I shipped a
REACHABILITY guard instead: it samples the live scorer's true maximum, compares it to every regime
threshold, and states plainly when the bar is set above anything the scorer can produce. The number
is your decision, not a bug fix.

One more thing worth knowing: P3B's own synthesis concluded that 8 of 8 powered regimes carry
measured non-stationary structure -- sign flips -- and said in its own words "not an absent signal, a
moving target; a single fixed-window linear search cannot capture this by design." That is the EA
reaching your reframing independently, by a different route, on the same afternoon.

Build SLS(181), four compiles today, 0 errors 0 warnings each, byte-identical across all four
locations. Sessions 57-61 in the ledger. No criterion claimed today -- 33 of 45.
